standard.title: Solving One-Variable Linear Equations
standard.description: solve one-variable linear equations with natural number solutions; verify the solution by substitution
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can find unknown values in equations using backtracking and balance (from AC9M6A02). Students can formulate algebraic expressions (from AC9M7A02).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students solve one-variable linear equations with natural number solutions using algebraic methods and verify solutions by substitution.

nodes.label: Equation as a balance statement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students understand that an equation is a statement of equality and that the solution is the value that makes it true.
nodes.minimum_width: Use substitution to check whether a given value is the solution to a simple equation.
nodes.typical_width: Explain what it means to 'solve' an equation; test multiple candidates for a solution; distinguish between expressions and equations.
wider: Investigate equations that have no natural number solution vs those that do — develop the habit of verifying.
Use a balance model to demonstrate what 'maintaining equality' means concretely.

response_modes.reason: Students often confuse solving an equation with simplifying an expression. Multiple contexts and the explicit distinction between 'expression' and 'equation' help establish this foundational understanding.

success_criteria: Correctly identifies whether a given value satisfies an equation by substitution.
Distinguishes between an expression and an equation.
Understands that a solution must make both sides equal.

nodes.label: Solving by backtracking
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students solve one-step and two-step linear equations by backtracking (undoing operations in reverse order).
nodes.minimum_width: Solve equations of the form ax = b and x + a = b by backtracking; show the inverse operations used.
nodes.typical_width: Solve two-step equations (e.g. 3x + 7 = 19) using backtracking; explain the process at each step.
wider: Compare backtracking and the balance/algebraic method for the same equation — note they produce the same result.
Apply to contextual problems: write and solve an equation from a word problem.

response_modes.reason: Backtracking requires students to map the order of operations forward then reverse it. An explicit scaffold (draw the 'machine', identify steps, reverse) is needed before students apply this fluently.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot execute the backtracking scaffold cannot transition to the algebraic balance method in Node 3 — both methods require identifying the order of operations, and the backtracking scaffold makes this explicit before the abstract method is introduced.
success_criteria: Correctly solves a two-step linear equation using backtracking.
Applies backtracking to multi-operation equations in the correct order.

nodes.label: Solving algebraically and verifying
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students solve one-variable linear equations algebraically, using the balance model, and verify the solution by substitution.
nodes.minimum_width: Solve a two-step linear equation algebraically (performing the same operation to both sides) and verify by substitution.
nodes.typical_width: Solve a range of one-variable linear equations; choose between backtracking and algebraic methods; always verify.
wider: Create and solve equations from contextual problems (e.g. 'I think of a number, double it and add 5 to get 19').
Investigate equations where the unknown appears in a context requiring interpretation of the solution (e.g. 'x must be a whole number of people').

response_modes.reason: Algebraic solving and verification together form the method students need to have automatic before applying equations to modelling contexts. The verification habit specifically needs consolidation.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who lack automatic algebraic solving and the verification habit cannot apply equations to modelling problems in AC9M7N09 and AC9M7M06 — the modelling contexts require fluent solving, and missing verification means errors go undetected.
success_criteria: Solves a one-variable linear equation algebraically with correct steps shown.
Verifies the solution by substituting back into the original equation.
